facts.label: Version relationships and conflicts
facts.text: - Credit Agreement amendments are described, not supplied. They are Amendment No. 1 (November 29, 2024), No. 2 (December 13, 2024), No. 3 (May 2, 2025) and No. 4 (October 15, 2025). Each is a separate active instrument, and none of the documents is available to verify the notes. - Revolver maturity timing: the Q3 10-Q states the "$220 in revolving commitments that matured on October 7, 2026" (page:25) and still lists "$953 million" revolver availability "as of September 30, 2026" (page:149). The commitment matured after the balance-sheet date and before the as-of date. This is a subsequent event relative to September 30, 2026. The filings do not say whether the $220 million tranche was extended or replaced. Availability after October 7, 2026 is therefore not established. Downstream use must keep the balance-sheet-date figure and the post-balance-sheet maturity apart. Severity high for CP-1 and CP-2. - Total debt principal: the Q3 10-Q table shows "Total debt principal" of 3,872 at September 30, 2026 and 4,182 at December 31, 2025 (page:24). The Q3 release Net Leverage reconciliation shows 3,872 and, in the comparative column, 4,185 (Q3 release page:13). The comparative column is not December 31, 2025, so the two do not conflict, but the release and the 10-Q use different comparison dates. Period labels need care. Severity low. - Depreciation and amortization: the Q3 release cash flow statement shows 259 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025 (page:10), while the Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation shows 236 for the same nine months (page:13). The release footnote on the twelve months ended September 30, 2025 attributes accelerated depreciation to the restructuring caption (page:16). This is a labelled presentation difference and is not resolved here. It is flagged for CP-1A and CP-2. - Liquidity: the Q3 release gives "Total liquidity was $1.7 billion" built from unrestricted cash and revolver capacity (page:4). The 10-Q gives its components at page:149. The release rounds, so the 10-Q controls the components. - Prior-period revision: see the earnings release finding above. The scale of the revision is not stated in the Q3 release text. Locate it in the 10-K before using any 2025 comparative. - Management claims such as "Net Leverage ratio of approximately 4.3x" (Q3 release, page:4) are management-defined non-GAAP and attributed. They do not override the filings. The leverage definition uses unrestricted cash only and Adjusted EBITDA, which excludes litigation and environmental items.

facts.label: Reported basis and authority
facts.text: The 10-K is the audited source. The 10-Qs are the filed unaudited interim source and control over the releases. The earnings releases are issuer-authored and unaudited. Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted Net Income, Free Cash Flows and Net Leverage Ratio are management-defined non-GAAP measures and are shown as attributed claims only. Management defines Net Leverage Ratio as total debt principal less unrestricted cash and cash equivalents, divided by Adjusted EBITDA (Q3 ER page:12). FY2025 and FY2024 amounts are as revised in the 10-K ("management concluded that the amounts are not material", 10-K page:166), and the 10-K revision tables show the FY2024 revisions (10-K page:167 to page:168). The Q3 ER repeats that prior-period amounts were revised (Q3 ER page:2).

facts.label: Debt composition as reported
facts.text: Revolving Credit Facility: aggregate commitments were 1,000 comprising 780 maturing May 2, 2030 and 220 that "matured on October 7, 2026" (Q3 10-Q page:25). It has a springing maturity if the term loans or the 2028 and 2029 notes are not refinanced within the 91 days before their maturity (page:25). Letters of credit of 47 were outstanding and no borrowings (page:26). The 10-K discloses a revolver-only maximum senior secured net leverage ratio of 2.00 to 1.00 (10-K page:211) and the Third Amendment increased the quarterly maintenance test "through the fiscal quarter ended September 30, 2026" (Q3 10-Q page:25). The Q3 10-Q states compliance at September 30, 2026 (page:149). The test level in force from the fourth quarter of 2026 is not stated in the supplied text. Other facilities: a receivables securitization facility with a 165 limit extended to March 31, 2028 (Q3 10-Q page:27) and a European factoring facility up to EUR 180 million (10-K page:218).

facts.label: Interpretation of what the evidence supports
facts.text: - Leverage: management net leverage fell during 2026 as debt was repaid with proceeds of the Kuan Yin land sales, but it remains high and the year-end target was moved up in successive releases. The full-year Adjusted EBITDA range was cut twice and the leverage target moved from below 3.8x to below 4.2x (Q1 ER, Q2 ER and Q3 ER outlook pages above). The calculation bridge recomputes the ratio from filed debt and the stated LTM Adjusted EBITDA. - Earnings quality: Q3 2026 reported net income of 196 was helped by a 150 receipt under the PFAS Insurance MOU booked as a reduction to SG&A (Q3 10-Q page:2) and by a 50 gain on land sales (Q3 10-Q page:133). Management excludes both from Adjusted EBITDA through the litigation-related income and gain lines (Q3 ER page:13). Adjusted EBITDA of 200 therefore rests on operating pricing in Titanium Technologies and Advanced Performance Materials, offset by a decline in Thermal & Specialized Solutions Adjusted EBITDA of 58 year over year (Q3 ER page:11). The 150 receipt is restricted cash held for New Jersey settlement payments (Q3 10-Q page:155), so it is not free liquidity. - Cash flow: nine-month cash from operations of 263 includes the 150 receipt and about 100 of related settlement payments (Q3 ER page:17), and land-sale tax payments of about 25 in Q3 (Q3 ER page:5). Free cash flow of 119 for nine months is management-defined. Cash taxes and cash interest for 2026 interim periods are not supplied. - Liquidity: unrestricted cash and revolver availability reported at September 30, 2026 are 698 and 953 (Q3 10-Q page:149). A 220 commitment tranche matured on October 7, 2026, after the balance-sheet date and before the as-of date, and the supplied text does not say what availability is after it. Management states sources of liquidity are sufficient "through at least the end of November 2027" (Q3 10-Q page:156). - Maturity profile: no maturity falls before 2028 in the Q3 debt table other than small amortization and finance items. The euro term loan (153) and 2028 notes (595) mature in 2028, the 2029 notes (620) in 2029. The 10-K disclosed the revolver springing-maturity feature that keys on those dates (Q3 10-Q page:25). The 10-K scheduled maturities at December 31, 2025 were 11, 505, 1,282, 631 and 10 for 2026 to 2030 (10-K page:106); the 505 and part of the 2028 amount have since been redeemed or repaid. - Contingent and environmental obligations outside debt: accrued litigation of 553 (191 current) and environmental remediation of 805 (116 current) at September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:155 and page:153). The North Carolina settlement totals 455 over 15 years, with a first payment of 51 in October 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:116). The remaining New Jersey payments are 176 on a net present value basis after the first 100 payment, and 150 of restricted cash is held to fund them (page:155). These are outside management's net debt measure. - Ratings: Moody's downgraded to B1 from Ba3 on July 17, 2026 with a stable outlook; the S&P statement in the filing is a BB- affirmation with negative outlook dated April 16, 2025 (Q3 10-Q page:149). A newer S&P action is not in the sources. - Capital returns: a quarterly dividend of 0.0875 per share was declared on October 27, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:156). Dividends paid were 39 in nine months 2026 against 63 in nine months 2025 (Q3 10-Q page:5).

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: On March 12, 2026 the company closed a private offering of 7.875% senior notes due 2034 in an aggregate principal amount of 700, issued under the 2020 base indenture as supplemented by a Fourth Supplemental Indenture, with a guarantor named in the agreement but not named in the supplied text (Q3 10-Q page:27). Use of proceeds: together with cash on hand, the redemption of 188 of the 5.750% senior notes due 2028 and the redemption of all 495 of the 5.375% senior notes due 2027 (Q3 10-Q page:27). This addressed the nearest unsecured maturity: the 10-K had warned that "the Company would not have sufficient funds to repay this indebtedness at maturity absent refinancing or other capital-raising actions" (10-K page:170). The refinancing extended the unsecured maturity profile at a higher stated coupon than the notes it replaced. The coupon comparison is a documentary comparison of two stated rates and not a cost-of-debt analysis.

These are cash obligations that compete with debt service. Management's net leverage measure does not include them (CP-1 handoff, obligations outside management net debt).

Behaviour category: Supportive or Neutral on the documented actions, with the caveat that willingness is separate from legal capacity and feasibility. Legal capacity to pay dividends, make restricted payments or incur debt depends on the Credit Agreement and indenture baskets, which are not supplied (Insufficient Information). Feasibility is constrained by the leverage and liquidity facts in CP-1.

facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: 1. Revenue durability: evidence is the mix of regulation-driven Opteon demand, TiO2 pricing actions and growth in Performance Solutions (10-K page:12; Q3 ER page:3 to page:4). Risk mechanic: TSS aftermarket volume fell year over year after a prior-year channel fill, which lowers TSS earnings that carried the group, while TT improvement depends on price increases holding. Credit implication: earnings visibility is moderate and depends on TiO2 pricing and the TSS aftermarket cycle, with the fourth-quarter guidance pointing to seasonal softness (Q3 ER page:5). Counter-evidence logged: the guidance cuts across Q1 to Q3 releases. 2. Margin and cash flow risk: evidence is the reconciliation of Adjusted EBITDA to reported results, where large litigation, environmental and land-sale items are excluded (Q3 ER page:13). Risk mechanic: management earnings measures exclude items that consume cash over time. Credit implication: leverage measured on Adjusted EBITDA understates cash claims; CP-2 should present metrics before and after these items. 3. Liquidity and refinancing: evidence is the 2034 notes refinancing, the matured 220 revolver tranche, the springing maturity feature and the 2028 and 2029 maturities (Q3 10-Q page:25, page:27). Risk mechanic: a springing maturity ties revolver availability to refinancing of the 2028 and 2029 debt. Credit implication: refinancing risk concentrates in 2028 and 2029; the next debt actions determine revolver access. 4. Concentration: low single-customer concentration (10-K page:6) but material dependence on a few regulation- and price-driven products. Credit implication: moderate concentration risk by product line, not by customer. 5. Sponsor alignment: not applicable, no sponsor identified. Key uncertainties: legal capacity under financing documents, guarantor structure, post-October 7 revolver capacity and the size and timing of legacy settlement payments.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Chemours is a stretched but liquid credit: near-term debt service looks manageable, while leverage and legacy obligations are the weak points. Its strongest support is USD 698 million of unrestricted cash, no revolver borrowings, no bond or term loan maturity of size before 2028 and a TiO2 price recovery that lifted third-quarter 2026 Adjusted EBITDA to USD 200 million. Its weakest point is management net leverage of about 4.3x, which leaves out USD 1,358 million of litigation and environmental reserves, with LTM interest cover of about 2.7x. The outcome turns on whether TiO2 pricing holds, whether the cooling aftermarket stabilises, and how the 2028 and 2029 refinancing meets settlement payments. Confidence is Medium.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: The refinancing in March 2026 changed the shape of the debt. The company issued USD 700 million of 7.875% senior notes due 2034 and used the proceeds with cash to retire the notes due 2027 and part of the notes due 2028, so the next material maturities are the 2028 euro term loan and notes and the 2029 notes, together about USD 1,368 million, or about 35% of USD 3,872 million of debt principal [CP-1 debt table; Calculations]. This removes a near-term wall that the 10-K had flagged as unfunded absent refinancing, at the price of a higher stated coupon on the replacement paper than on the notes retired.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Leverage fell during 2026 but remains high, and management's own targets slipped. Management net leverage was about 4.9x at March 31, about 4.4x at June 30 and about 4.3x at September 30, 2026, driven by debt repaid from Kuan Yin land-sale proceeds rather than by earnings growth [CP-1 quarterly trajectory]. Over the same releases the full-year Adjusted EBITDA range was cut from USD 800 to 900 million to USD 775 to 800 million and the year-end leverage target moved from below 3.8x to below 4.2x. A creditor should treat the improvement as asset-sale deleveraging, which cannot repeat once the land is sold.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Earnings quality is weaker than the headline. Third-quarter 2026 net income of USD 196 million includes a USD 150 million insurance-related receipt booked against SG&A and a USD 50 million land gain, and full-year GAAP results include a USD 307 million nine-month tax provision after a full valuation allowance [CP-1 financials table]. Adjusted EBITDA of USD 200 million excludes these items, but it also excludes litigation and environmental charges that consume cash over 15 to 25 years. Segment mix has shifted: Titanium Technologies Adjusted EBITDA rose to USD 85 million from USD 25 million on price, while Thermal and Specialized Solutions fell to USD 136 million from USD 194 million as the stationary aftermarket normalised after prior-year channel fill [CP-1 segment table].

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Legacy obligations sit outside the leverage ratio and compete with debt service. Accrued litigation of USD 553 million and environmental remediation of USD 805 million at September 30, 2026 are not debt, yet the New Jersey order (USD 875 million over 25 years) and the North Carolina settlement (USD 455 million over 15 years, first payment of USD 51 million in October 2026) require annual cash [CP-1A transaction summary]. Part is funded by a USD 150 million insurance escrow and shared with DuPont and Corteva under the 2021 MOU, up to a cap. Including the reserves in debt on an illustrative basis raises leverage to about 6.1x (Calculations); that is a sensitivity, not a measure management or any covenant uses.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: Liquidity is adequate on the balance-sheet date but its second leg is uncertain. Unrestricted cash of USD 698 million plus revolver availability of USD 953 million gave USD 1,651 million at September 30, 2026. A USD 220 million revolving tranche matured on October 7, 2026, and the filings do not say whether it was extended. If it was not, arithmetic availability would be USD 733 million. The revolver also carries a springing maturity linked to the 2028 and 2029 debt, so access to the revolver depends on that refinancing being completed in advance.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. Liquidity is solid at the reporting date: USD 698 million of unrestricted cash, no revolver borrowings and USD 953 million of availability, with management stating that sources are sufficient through at least the end of November 2027 [Management Language, CP-1 liquidity bridge]. The maturity profile has been extended: the senior secured term loan in dollars is due in October 2032 and no bond matures before November 2028 [Documentary Fact]. Customer concentration is low, with no customer above 10% of net sales and about 2,400 customers across about 110 countries [Documentary Fact, CP-1A]. Demand drivers are partly regulatory (AIM Act and F-Gas transitions to Opteon) and partly price-led recovery in TiO2, with growth in Performance Solutions serving data center and semiconductor markets [Documentary Fact for the regulation, Management Language for growth claims]. The company has acted creditor-supportively on capital allocation, cutting the dividend and repaying debt from asset sales [Documentary Fact, CP-1A].

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Weaknesses. Leverage is high on any basis shown and the improvement came from asset-sale proceeds [Analyst Interpretation, CP-1 bridges]. Legacy PFAS and environmental liabilities are large, multi-decade and uncertain in scale, and only part is cost-shared [Documentary Fact]. Earnings are concentrated in a cyclical product (TiO2) and a regulation-timed product (Opteon aftermarket) whose year-over-year trend turned negative in the third quarter [Documentary Fact, Analyst Interpretation]. Reported GAAP results are volatile because of litigation, valuation allowance and gain items, which complicates covenant and add-back reading [Documentary Fact]. The financing documents are not in the pack, so guarantor coverage, restricted-payment capacity and covenant headroom cannot be verified [Insufficient Information]. A history of restated prior periods and a past Audit Committee review raise the weight a creditor should place on reconciling adjusted measures to filings [Documentary Fact, Analyst Interpretation].

No market data, quotes or spreads; S&P action stale
Ownership and holder detail not disclosed
Fixed versus variable cost structure and contract share of revenue not disclosed
Illustrative leverage including reserves mixes discounted and undiscounted items

spans.text: ## Request

Module CP-0, source readiness, for The Chemours Company (issuer id cc, NYSE: CC), pathway credit_snapshot, as-of date 2026-11-05, cutoff 2026-11-05, current period q3-2026, prior period fy-2025, reporting currency USD. The selected downstream consumers are CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2 and CP-5 (the minimum module set). The question answered here is whether the supplied source set can support those consumers and what remains blocked. This is a source-sufficiency review only (SOURCE_SUFFICIENCY_ONLY). It contains no credit conclusion, no legal interpretation and no normalization or reconciliation of figures. Quarter, year-to-date and LTM figures quoted below are located-evidence pointers, not accepted model inputs.

Page locators use the `page:N` index of the converted-text source files supplied to this run. That index is an extraction chunk, not the printed filing page. Where a printed page is quoted it is labelled as such.

### Supplied handoffs

### Ignored input
`_retrieval.json` was ignored by CP-OS and is not relied on. It is a retrieval log, not issuer evidence.
## Findings
### Overall readiness answer

The seven issuer filings support the four selected consumers, with bounded limitations. No source has blocked preparation. Every source has extracted text (see Extraction status). The set covers the audited FY2025 base, three interim periods in 2026 and three matching earnings releases. The set contains no executed legal financing documents and no presentation decks. Debt terms therefore come only from the notes to the filed statements. The weakest areas are covenant definitions, guarantor detail and cash-paid interest and tax for interim periods. Those are gaps for CP-1 and CP-2 and do not stop either one. Source sufficiency is a separate matter from completion of downstream analysis. Nothing here says that CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2 or CP-5 has been done.
### Source-by-source assessment
#### Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025

Identity and period are established from content. The cover reads "For the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025" and gives "Commission File Number 001-36794" for "The Chemours Company" (page:1). Original authority is the filed, audited annual report. Its debt note is "Note 20 – Debt" (cross-referenced from page:102) and holds facility-level terms, guarantee wording, redemption terms and the securitization and factoring facilities (page:211 to page:218). The scheduled-maturity discussion in Liquidity and Capital Resources is at page:106. The 10-K shows the Revolving Credit Facility terms: "$780 in revolving commitments that mature on May 2, 2030 and $220 in revolving commitments that mature on October 7, 2026" (page:211). It also states a springing-maturity feature and a revolver-only maintenance test, "a maximum senior secured net leverage ratio of 2.00 to 1.00" (page:211). Cash paid for interest and income taxes appears in the supplemental cash-flow information at page:163 ("Interest, net of amounts capitalized" and "Income taxes, net of refunds"). The converted text is a text rendering of HTML and carries no images or speaker notes.
#### Forms 10-Q for Q1, Q2 and Q3 2026

Each cover states its quarterly period (March 31, 2026; June 30, 2026; September 30, 2026; page:1 of each file). Each is unaudited and consolidated. The Q3 10-Q is the latest financial report and the primary authority for the September 30, 2026 balance sheet, debt table (Note 15, page:24), the liquidity discussion (page:148 to page:150) and segment note (Note 23, page:130 to page:134). The three 10-Qs are separate active sources and are not collapsed. The Q3 10-Q supersedes the earlier ones only for September 30, 2026 balances. The earlier 10-Qs remain the only filed support for the March and June 2026 balances and for discrete-quarter derivation.
#### Earnings releases (Q1, Q2, Q3 2026)

These are issuer-authored, unaudited and sit below the filings in authority. They provide reported and adjusted figures, a non-GAAP reconciliation, free cash flow, guidance and attributed management narrative. The Q3 release has a Net Leverage Ratio reconciliation and outlook (page:13, page:5 and page:6). Their non-GAAP measures must be carried as management-defined and must not override the filings. The Q3 release also states that "Certain prior period amounts have been revised to correct for certain immaterial errors as further described in our Annual Report on Form 10-K for the year ended December 31, 2025" (Q3 release, page:2). Prior-period comparatives therefore carry a revision flag that CP-1A must resolve against the 10-K.
### Coverage by profile
#### Financial reports

Statements, notes, segment tables, debt and liquidity are retained in the 10-K and the three 10-Qs. Segment data is in Note 23 of the Q3 10-Q (page:130 to page:134) and in the segment reconciliation (page:147). The debt table with facility-level principal and carrying adjustments is at page:24 of the Q3 10-Q. Liquidity, restricted cash and covenant compliance language are at page:148 to page:150. The Q3 10-Q states "At September 30, 2026, we were in compliance with the applicable covenants under the Credit Agreement" (page:149). No leverage covenant levels, threshold schedules or headroom calculations were located in the Q3 10-Q beyond the 10-K statement for the revolver.
#### Earnings releases

Each release carries reported figures, an adjusted reconciliation, quarter and year-to-date columns, and outlook. Quarter versus year-to-date and twelve-month columns are separately labelled in the Q3 release reconciliation (page:12 and page:13). Adjusted EBITDA, Adjusted Net Income, Free Cash Flows and Net Leverage Ratio are non-GAAP and management-defined.
#### Legal and financing sources

Not supplied as documents. The Credit Agreement (dated August 18, 2023, with four amendments described in the filings), the 2020 Base Indenture and its supplements, the securitization Receivables Purchase Agreement and the European factoring agreement are described only in filing notes (Q3 10-Q page:24 to page:27; 10-K page:211 to page:218). The filings give amendments, dates, margins and maturities, but not defined terms, baskets, negative covenant detail, springing-maturity mechanics, release of guarantees or the Credit Agreement EBITDA definition. Those facts are gaps, not inferences. Guarantor wording exists only in note summaries (for example, guarantees "by each of the Company's existing and future direct and indirect domestic restricted subsidiaries that (i) incurs or guarantees indebtedness under the Senior Secured Credit Facilities", 10-K page:212).
#### Workbooks, scans, images and decks

None supplied. No presentation decks are in the pack, which uses earnings releases in place of decks. No claim is made about charts, images or speaker notes. Nothing in the pack required that coverage.
### Entity and instrument roles located

- Issuer and registrant: The Chemours Company (Delaware, "Commission File Number 001-36794"). It is also the borrower under the Credit Agreement as described in the filings. The context leaves borrower and parent blank, and the filings do not show a separate parent. Parent: none located.

- Guarantors: described generically as domestic restricted subsidiaries. No named subsidiary guarantor list was located in the supplied text. One guarantor is mentioned for the 2034 notes ("the guarantor named therein", Q3 10-Q page:27) without a name in the supplied text. Named guarantor identity is an unresolved distinction and a gap.

- Instruments in the Q3 10-Q debt table (page:24): Tranche B-4 U.S. dollar term loan due October 2032, Tranche B-3 euro term loan due August 2028, senior unsecured notes due 2028, 2029, 2033 and 2034, finance leases, a financing obligation, a supplier financing obligation and other debt. The 5.375% notes due May 2027 show no balance at September 30, 2026 because they were redeemed (page:27).
- Revolver: the Revolving Credit Facility, with "No borrowings were outstanding under the Revolving Credit Facility at September 30, 2026 and December 31, 2025" (page:26).

- Receivables facilities: a receivables securitization facility run through a special purpose entity (page:27 of the Q3 10-Q) and a European factoring arrangement with BNP Paribas Factor GmbH (10-K page:218). The filings treat these as sales of receivables, which matters for debt-like adjustments that CP-2 and CP-5 must decide on.
- Restricted versus unrestricted entities: the filings use "restricted subsidiaries" for guarantee language only. No unrestricted-subsidiary designation list was located. Not supplied.
### Version relationships and conflicts

- Credit Agreement amendments are described, not supplied. They are Amendment No. 1 (November 29, 2024), No. 2 (December 13, 2024), No. 3 (May 2, 2025) and No. 4 (October 15, 2025). Each is a separate active instrument, and none of the documents is available to verify the notes.

- Revolver maturity timing: the Q3 10-Q states the "$220 in revolving commitments that matured on October 7, 2026" (page:25) and still lists "$953 million" revolver availability "as of September 30, 2026" (page:149). The commitment matured after the balance-sheet date and before the as-of date. This is a subsequent event relative to September 30, 2026. The filings do not say whether the $220 million tranche was extended or replaced. Availability after October 7, 2026 is therefore not established. Downstream use must keep the balance-sheet-date figure and the post-balance-sheet maturity apart. Severity high for CP-1 and CP-2.

- Total debt principal: the Q3 10-Q table shows "Total debt principal" of 3,872 at September 30, 2026 and 4,182 at December 31, 2025 (page:24). The Q3 release Net Leverage reconciliation shows 3,872 and, in the comparative column, 4,185 (Q3 release page:13). The comparative column is not December 31, 2025, so the two do not conflict, but the release and the 10-Q use different comparison dates. Period labels need care. Severity low.

- Depreciation and amortization: the Q3 release cash flow statement shows 259 for the nine months ended September 30, 2025 (page:10), while the Adjusted EBITDA reconciliation shows 236 for the same nine months (page:13). The release footnote on the twelve months ended September 30, 2025 attributes accelerated depreciation to the restructuring caption (page:16). This is a labelled presentation difference and is not resolved here. It is flagged for CP-1A and CP-2.

- Liquidity: the Q3 release gives "Total liquidity was $1.7 billion" built from unrestricted cash and revolver capacity (page:4). The 10-Q gives its components at page:149. The release rounds, so the 10-Q controls the components.
- Prior-period revision: see the earnings release finding above. The scale of the revision is not stated in the Q3 release text. Locate it in the 10-K before using any 2025 comparative.

- Management claims such as "Net Leverage ratio of approximately 4.3x" (Q3 release, page:4) are management-defined non-GAAP and attributed. They do not override the filings. The leverage definition uses unrestricted cash only and Adjusted EBITDA, which excludes litigation and environmental items.
### Extraction status and fidelity

All seven files extracted to page-indexed text (counts above). Extraction status is not a fidelity review. Many tables in the converted text are flattened to one value per line, particularly in the releases, so row and column alignment must be checked against the label order before use. Percent signs and negative-number parentheses are split across lines in places. No image, chart or footnote-superscript fidelity is claimed. The 10-Q page index is a chunk index and does not match printed page numbers (for example the Q3 10-Q Item 2 begins at printed page 75 per its table of contents, but the liquidity discussion appears at page:148 of the chunk index).
### Consumer assessment
| Consumer | Evidence demand | Status | Reason |

Limitations: no executed credit agreement or indentures, no covenant level beyond the 10-K revolver test, revolver tranche that matured October 7, 2026, guarantor names, interim cash-paid interest and tax not located. |

If a later request needs covenant headroom, baskets, restricted-payment capacity or guarantee release mechanics, the Credit Agreement and indentures become required sources and the relevant consumer would turn CONDITIONAL.
### Model-input evidence (HTML Model objective)

Source evidence exists for discrete quarters (via three releases and three 10-Qs), fiscal year (10-K), quarter and year-to-date distinctions (labelled columns in the Q3 release at page:12 and page:13 and the 10-Q statements at page:2), segments (Q3 10-Q page:130 to page:134), add-backs (release reconciliations), KPIs (price and volume change tables, Q3 release page:12), facility-level debt carrying values (Q3 10-Q page:24) and business or transaction narrative. Cash-paid interest and tax are located for FY2025 only (10-K page:163). The assertion is SOURCE_SUFFICIENCY_ONLY; CP_MODEL_INPUT_CONTRACT_NOT_EVALUATED. No normalized quarter, reconciliation or input acceptance is asserted.

Evidence: the Q3 10-Q debt note and liquidity discussion give facility-level balances, covenant-compliance language and a revolver whose $220 million tranche "matured on October 7, 2026". Source risk mechanism: filing notes summarise rather than reproduce the executed agreements, and the filing's own balance-sheet-date availability may overstate availability on the as-of date. Downstream consequence: CP-1 and CP-2 can describe and measure the capital structure from the filings but must state that revolver availability after October 7, 2026, covenant headroom and guarantor identity are not established. The next evidence action is to obtain the Credit Agreement with Amendments No. 1 to No. 4 and the indentures, and to look for any filing after September 30, 2026 that addresses the matured revolver tranche.

### Interpretation of what the evidence supports

- Leverage: management net leverage fell during 2026 as debt was repaid with proceeds of the Kuan Yin land sales, but it remains high and the year-end target was moved up in successive releases. The full-year Adjusted EBITDA range was cut twice and the leverage target moved from below 3.8x to below 4.2x (Q1 ER, Q2 ER and Q3 ER outlook pages above). The calculation bridge recomputes the ratio from filed debt and the stated LTM Adjusted EBITDA.

- Earnings quality: Q3 2026 reported net income of 196 was helped by a 150 receipt under the PFAS Insurance MOU booked as a reduction to SG&A (Q3 10-Q page:2) and by a 50 gain on land sales (Q3 10-Q page:133). Management excludes both from Adjusted EBITDA through the litigation-related income and gain lines (Q3 ER page:13). Adjusted EBITDA of 200 therefore rests on operating pricing in Titanium Technologies and Advanced Performance Materials, offset by a decline in Thermal & Specialized Solutions Adjusted EBITDA of 58 year over year (Q3 ER page:11). The 150 receipt is restricted cash held for New Jersey settlement payments (Q3 10-Q page:155), so it is not free liquidity.

- Cash flow: nine-month cash from operations of 263 includes the 150 receipt and about 100 of related settlement payments (Q3 ER page:17), and land-sale tax payments of about 25 in Q3 (Q3 ER page:5). Free cash flow of 119 for nine months is management-defined. Cash taxes and cash interest for 2026 interim periods are not supplied.

- Liquidity: unrestricted cash and revolver availability reported at September 30, 2026 are 698 and 953 (Q3 10-Q page:149). A 220 commitment tranche matured on October 7, 2026, after the balance-sheet date and before the as-of date, and the supplied text does not say what availability is after it. Management states sources of liquidity are sufficient "through at least the end of November 2027" (Q3 10-Q page:156).

- Maturity profile: no maturity falls before 2028 in the Q3 debt table other than small amortization and finance items. The euro term loan (153) and 2028 notes (595) mature in 2028, the 2029 notes (620) in 2029. The 10-K disclosed the revolver springing-maturity feature that keys on those dates (Q3 10-Q page:25). The 10-K scheduled maturities at December 31, 2025 were 11, 505, 1,282, 631 and 10 for 2026 to 2030 (10-K page:106); the 505 and part of the 2028 amount have since been redeemed or repaid.

- Contingent and environmental obligations outside debt: accrued litigation of 553 (191 current) and environmental remediation of 805 (116 current) at September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:155 and page:153). The North Carolina settlement totals 455 over 15 years, with a first payment of 51 in October 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:116). The remaining New Jersey payments are 176 on a net present value basis after the first 100 payment, and 150 of restricted cash is held to fund them (page:155). These are outside management's net debt measure.

- Ratings: Moody's downgraded to B1 from Ba3 on July 17, 2026 with a stable outlook; the S&P statement in the filing is a BB- affirmation with negative outlook dated April 16, 2025 (Q3 10-Q page:149). A newer S&P action is not in the sources.

- Capital returns: a quarterly dividend of 0.0875 per share was declared on October 27, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:156). Dividends paid were 39 in nine months 2026 against 63 in nine months 2025 (Q3 10-Q page:5).

It also reviews governance and capital allocation behaviour at issuer level, using documented actions only. It gives no peer ranking, no instrument recommendation and no recovery conclusion. Figures are copied from sources or from the accepted CP-1 handoff and carry their locators. Locators are `page:N` of the converted-text source named (an extraction chunk, not the printed page). Fact tags used: Documentary Fact, Management Language, Analyst Interpretation, Insufficient Information.

| Management | Denise Dignam is President and Chief Executive Officer (as quoted in the release) | Documentary Fact | Q3 ER page:1 |

| Ratings | Moody's downgraded to B1 from Ba3 on July 17, 2026 with a stable outlook; the S&P reference in the filing is an April 16, 2025 affirmation of BB- with negative outlook, which is stale | Documentary Fact; stale S&P data | Q3 10-Q page:149 |

| Dividend and buyback policy | Quarterly dividend of 0.0875 per share declared on October 27, 2026; dividends declared per share were 0.5125 in FY2025 and 1.00 in FY2024; remaining repurchase authority of 441 million under the 2022 program at the date of the 10-K | Documentary Fact | Q3 10-Q page:156; 10-K page:162, page:110 |
| Controls and reporting | 2025 revisions of prior periods for immaterial errors; a 2024 Audit Committee internal review of reporting practices | Documentary Fact | 10-K page:166 to page:169 |
### Transaction summary and new debt issues

The supplied sources contain no sponsor transaction, merger or leveraged recapitalisation, and the context lists no deal terms. The transactions that matter to a creditor are a refinancing, debt paydown from asset-sale proceeds, a land sale, and legal settlements. This is a documentary summary. Figures reproduce CP-1 or cite a locator.

On March 12, 2026 the company closed a private offering of 7.875% senior notes due 2034 in an aggregate principal amount of 700, issued under the 2020 base indenture as supplemented by a Fourth Supplemental Indenture, with a guarantor named in the agreement but not named in the supplied text (Q3 10-Q page:27). Use of proceeds: together with cash on hand, the redemption of 188 of the 5.750% senior notes due 2028 and the redemption of all 495 of the 5.375% senior notes due 2027 (Q3 10-Q page:27). This addressed the nearest unsecured maturity: the 10-K had warned that "the Company would not have sufficient funds to repay this indebtedness at maturity absent refinancing or other capital-raising actions" (10-K page:170). The refinancing extended the unsecured maturity profile at a higher stated coupon than the notes it replaced. The coupon comparison is a documentary comparison of two stated rates and not a cost-of-debt analysis.

The company also repaid part of the euro term loan due August 2028 using land-sale proceeds and cash: EUR 140 million in April 2026 per the Q1 release, EUR 230 million in the second quarter per the Q2 release, and EUR 280 million in the nine months per the Q3 10-Q (Q1 ER page:4; Q2 ER page:5; Q3 10-Q page:26). The release amounts and the filing amount are labelled differently (April payment, quarter payment and nine-month total) and are logged here without reconciliation. A loss on extinguishment of debt is reported for the nine months (Q3 10-Q page:26). The debt balances after these actions are in the CP-1 handoff.

The Kuan Yin, Taiwan property: the company closed the site in 2023 as part of the Titanium Technologies Transformation Plan (Q3 10-Q page:16). In April 2026 it sold nine of ten land parcels for net proceeds of about 287 (Q1 ER page:4), and the Q3 release says the sale of the property was completed for total net consideration of about 340 including the remaining parcel for 56 of gross proceeds (Q3 ER page:1). A gain on sale of 316 for nine months 2026 is in the CP-1 handoff. About 25 of tax related to the sale was paid in Q3 (Q3 ER page:5). The proceeds are the stated source of debt reduction (Q1 ER page:1). Management Language: "positioning the Company to paydown" debt. This is a one-time source of liquidity and not recurring cash flow.

Legal settlements with cash consequences: a New Jersey judicial consent order was finalized in September 2026 with scheduled payments totalling 875 over 25 years, a first payment of 100 in September 2026, and a related PFAS Insurance MOU under which Corteva and DuPont funded 150 into an escrow for the company's New Jersey payments (Q3 10-Q page:155, page:39). A North Carolina settlement was entered in September 2026 with total payments of 455 over 15 years and a first payment of 51 in October 2026, which is a subsequent event relative to September 30, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:116). A June 2026 consent decree with the EPA and the West Virginia Department of Environmental Protection carries a 23 civil penalty and a commitment to fund 90 of projects over 15 years (Q3 10-Q page:111). These are cash obligations that compete with debt service. Management's net leverage measure does not include them (CP-1 handoff, obligations outside management net debt).

Other 2026 events: a 2026 Restructuring Program with employee separation charges was begun in the first quarter (Q3 10-Q page:14); the exit from the SPS Capstone business was completed in 2025 (Q2 ER page:2); an operational outage at the Washington Works site reduced APM volumes in the first half and was reported resolved by the second quarter (Q1 ER page:2; Q2 ER page:3); the company launched a liquid cooling portfolio under the Faizeon brand (Q3 ER page:1).

New debt issues and amendments: 7.875% senior notes due 2034, 700, closed March 12, 2026. Credit Agreement Amendment No. 4 in October 2025 extended the U.S. dollar term loan from August 2028 to October 2032 with a wider margin (Q3 10-Q page:26). Moody's downgrade followed on July 17, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:149). Documents for the notes and the amendments are not supplied, so covenant and guarantee terms remain unverified. Draft or unexecuted status: none of the described transactions is described as draft; the North Carolina settlement is described as entered into and its first payment as made after the quarter. A settlement in principle with about 2,900 private well owners is described as not final (Q3 10-Q page:116).
### Timeline of credit-relevant events
| Date | Event | Locator | Type |
| July 1, 2015 | Separation from EID | 10-K page:9 | History |
| January 2021 | MOU with DuPont, Corteva and EID on legacy PFAS cost sharing | Q3 10-Q page:35 | History |
| February 29, 2024 | Announced delay of 2023 year-end reporting pending an Audit Committee internal review | 10-K page:169 | History |
| August 2025 | Agreement with New Jersey and PFAS Insurance MOU entered | Q3 10-Q page:39 | History |
| October 15, 2025 | Credit Agreement Amendment No. 4 | Q3 10-Q page:25 to page:26 | Refinancing |
| February 24, 2026 | 10-K audit report date and filing of FY2025 results | 10-K page:160 | Reporting |
| March 12, 2026 | 7.875% senior notes due 2034 issued; 2027 notes redeemed and part of 2028 notes redeemed | Q3 10-Q page:27 | Refinancing |
| April to September 2026 | Kuan Yin parcel sales; euro term loan repaid in part | Q1 ER page:4; Q3 10-Q page:26 | Disposal and deleveraging |
| June 2026 | EPA and WVDEP consent decree; full valuation allowance on U.S. deferred tax assets concluded in Q2 | Q3 10-Q page:111; Q3 ER page:15 | Regulatory and tax |
| July 17, 2026 | Moody's downgrade to B1 | Q3 10-Q page:149 | Rating |
| September 2026 | New Jersey consent order finalized; North Carolina settlement; MOU escrow funding obligations deemed satisfied | Q3 10-Q page:38 to page:39 | Legal |
| October 7, 2026 | 220 revolving commitments tranche matured (subsequent event to the September 30 balance sheet) | Q3 10-Q page:25 | Subsequent event |
| October 2026 | First North Carolina settlement payment of 51 (subsequent event) | Q3 10-Q page:116 | Subsequent event |
| October 27, 2026 | Fourth quarter dividend declared (subsequent event) | Q3 10-Q page:156 | Subsequent event |
### Governance and capital allocation behaviour (issuer level)

Documented actions only; no scoring is stated here. Dividends declared fell from 1.00 per share in FY2024 to 0.5125 in FY2025 and to a quarterly 0.0875 in 2026 (10-K page:162; Q3 10-Q page:156), and the company used land-sale proceeds and cash to repay debt (Q1 ER page:1; Q3 10-Q page:26). These are deleveraging actions that support creditors. Capital returned in the nine months of 2026 was 39 in dividends and none in buybacks (CP-1 handoff). Behaviour category: Supportive or Neutral on the documented actions, with the caveat that willingness is separate from legal capacity and feasibility. Legal capacity to pay dividends, make restricted payments or incur debt depends on the Credit Agreement and indenture baskets, which are not supplied (Insufficient Information). Feasibility is constrained by the leverage and liquidity facts in CP-1.

Reporting integrity: the company revised prior periods for immaterial errors that affected costs of goods sold timing and income tax expense (10-K page:166 to page:167), and an Audit Committee internal review covered the Ethics Hotline process, working capital practices and certain non-GAAP metrics (10-K page:169). The 10-K lists regulatory inquiries and litigation that may arise from that review as a risk (10-K page:4). The supplied text does not say that a material weakness was identified; this is not established either way beyond the risk-factor language, so it is Insufficient Information. Mechanism: reliability of reported adjusted measures and add-backs matters because leverage covenants and management leverage ratios depend on them.

Legacy liabilities: the company carries large environmental and litigation reserves that it describes as arising from pre-spin-off activities of its former parent, cost-shared under the MOU subject to an aggregate cap (Q3 10-Q page:35, page:153). Mechanism: cash settlements are paid over 15 to 25 years and are not classified as debt, which can reduce cash available for debt service and for refinancing without changing reported leverage. Implication for monitoring: track annual settlement payments against free cash flow.
### Conflicts logged (not reconciled)

- Debt paydown amounts: Q1 ER says the company paid down EUR 140 million in April 2026 (Q1 ER page:4); the Q2 ER says EUR 230 million was paid down in the second quarter (Q2 ER page:5); the Q3 10-Q says EUR 280 million was used in the nine months, of which EUR 50 million in the third quarter (Q3 10-Q page:26). The labelled periods differ (April, quarter, nine months), and the sums are not reconciled here.

- Kuan Yin consideration: Q1 ER reports about 287 of initial net proceeds from nine of ten parcels (Q1 ER page:4); Q3 ER reports total net consideration of about 340 including the last parcel for 56 of gross proceeds (Q3 ER page:1). The measures differ (initial net versus total net versus gross) and are logged as stated.

- Revolver availability: the Q3 10-Q reports availability of 953 at September 30, 2026 and also that 220 of commitments matured on October 7, 2026 (Q3 10-Q page:149). The post-maturity availability is not stated.

- Full-year guidance moved between releases, with Adjusted EBITDA of 800 to 900 (Q1 ER page:6), 775 to 825 (Q2 ER page:6) and 775 to 800 (Q3 ER page:6). This is a change in management expectations and not a conflict of fact.
### Credit translations

1. Revenue durability: evidence is the mix of regulation-driven Opteon demand, TiO2 pricing actions and growth in Performance Solutions (10-K page:12; Q3 ER page:3 to page:4). Risk mechanic: TSS aftermarket volume fell year over year after a prior-year channel fill, which lowers TSS earnings that carried the group, while TT improvement depends on price increases holding. Credit implication: earnings visibility is moderate and depends on TiO2 pricing and the TSS aftermarket cycle, with the fourth-quarter guidance pointing to seasonal softness (Q3 ER page:5). Counter-evidence logged: the guidance cuts across Q1 to Q3 releases.

2. Margin and cash flow risk: evidence is the reconciliation of Adjusted EBITDA to reported results, where large litigation, environmental and land-sale items are excluded (Q3 ER page:13). Risk mechanic: management earnings measures exclude items that consume cash over time. Credit implication: leverage measured on Adjusted EBITDA understates cash claims; CP-2 should present metrics before and after these items.

3. Liquidity and refinancing: evidence is the 2034 notes refinancing, the matured 220 revolver tranche, the springing maturity feature and the 2028 and 2029 maturities (Q3 10-Q page:25, page:27). Risk mechanic: a springing maturity ties revolver availability to refinancing of the 2028 and 2029 debt. Credit implication: refinancing risk concentrates in 2028 and 2029; the next debt actions determine revolver access.

4. Concentration: low single-customer concentration (10-K page:6) but material dependence on a few regulation- and price-driven products. Credit implication: moderate concentration risk by product line, not by customer.

5. Sponsor alignment: not applicable, no sponsor identified. Key uncertainties: legal capacity under financing documents, guarantor structure, post-October 7 revolver capacity and the size and timing of legacy settlement payments.
### Consumer readiness
| Consumer | What it should take from CP-1A | Why it matters | Gap | Action |

| CP-2 | The refinancing history, springing maturity linkage, obligations outside management net debt, the matured revolver tranche, and the dividend and repayment behaviour | Credit metrics should be shown with and without legacy settlement cash and with the revolver caveat | Executed financing documents, post-October 7 availability, interim cash taxes and interest | Use the filed amounts and carry the caveats; no covenant headroom from filing text |

| CP-5 | The business description, segment drivers, timeline and transaction summary | The report profile and transaction sections draw directly on these rows | Ownership detail, named guarantors, fixed versus variable cost split, contract share of revenue | Mark these as not supplied in the report |
## Calculations

None performed in CP-1A. Numeric facts are quoted from sources with locators or reproduced from the accepted CP-1 handoff. Comparisons of coupons, amounts or dates above are statements of two stated values and not derived figures. No new calculation, and therefore no new inputs, exist to list.
## Gaps
| Gap | Severity | Affected | Action |

| Holder names, ownership percentages and any control rights are not disclosed in the supplied sources | Medium | CP-5, governance | Treat ownership as Insufficient Information; do not infer from share counts |

| Credit Agreement, indentures and guarantor schedules not supplied, so legal capacity for distributions, debt incurrence and asset sales is unknown | High | CP-2 | Obtain the documents before judging restricted payment capacity |
| Post-October 7, 2026 revolver availability and any replacement of the matured 220 tranche not stated | High | CP-2 | Look for a later filing |
| Fixed versus variable cost split, contract share of revenue and pass-through of input cost not disclosed | Medium | Margin and revenue visibility | State as not disclosed |
| No presentation decks or call transcripts in the pack; management narrative comes from releases | Low | CP-5 | Label management language as such |

| Outcome of the 2024 Audit Committee review and any control deficiency conclusions are only partly in the supplied text (the 10-K discussion is a summary) | Medium | Reporting integrity | Read the controls section before concluding |
| Debt paydown and land-sale amounts are reported on different bases across the releases and the 10-Q | Low | Transaction summary | Keep the labels; no reconciliation |
| Latest S&P action not supplied | Low | Ratings | Treat as stale |
| Settlement terms are as summarised in filing notes; the underlying agreements are not supplied | Medium | Legacy liabilities | Treat payment schedules as disclosed, not verified |
## Next module

CP-2, then CP-5. CP-2 takes the leverage, coverage and liquidity facts from CP-1 and the refinancing and legacy-settlement context here. CP-5 composes the company profile and transaction summary from this handoff and must carry the ownership, guarantor and legal-document gaps.

## Findings
### Credit view

Chemours is a stretched but liquid credit: near-term debt service looks manageable, while leverage and legacy obligations are the weak points. Its strongest support is USD 698 million of unrestricted cash, no revolver borrowings, no bond or term loan maturity of size before 2028 and a TiO2 price recovery that lifted third-quarter 2026 Adjusted EBITDA to USD 200 million. Its weakest point is management net leverage of about 4.3x, which leaves out USD 1,358 million of litigation and environmental reserves, with LTM interest cover of about 2.7x. The outcome turns on whether TiO2 pricing holds, whether the cooling aftermarket stabilises, and how the 2028 and 2029 refinancing meets settlement payments. Confidence is Medium.
### Credit assessment
| Item | Assessment | Category | Confidence | Basis |

| Fundamental credit view | Stretched leverage with adequate near-term liquidity; legacy settlement cash and the 2028 to 2029 refinancing are the main swing factors | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1 financial tables and bridges; CP-1A refinancing, timeline and credit translations |

| Business risk | Moderate: low customer concentration and regulation-supported refrigerant demand, offset by cyclical TiO2 pricing and TSS aftermarket normalisation | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | CP-1A company and operating model rows; CP-1 segment table |

| Financial risk | High: management net leverage of about 4.3x on LTM Adjusted EBITDA, gross leverage above 5x, thin interest and capex coverage | Documentary Fact for the inputs; Analyst Interpretation for the reading | Medium | CP-1 debt and leverage bridge; Calculations below |

| Liquidity | Adequate at September 30, 2026; post-October 7, 2026 revolver capacity not stated | Documentary Fact; Insufficient Information for post-maturity capacity | Medium | CP-1 liquidity bridge; CP-1A subsequent events |

| Sponsor and governance | No sponsor identified; deleveraging and lower dividends are supportive documented actions; legal capacity for distributions not verifiable | Analyst Interpretation; Insufficient Information for legal capacity | Low | CP-1A governance rows |

Confidence is below High because CP-1A and CP-0 record that executed financing documents are not supplied, that revolver capacity after the October 7, 2026 maturity of the 220 tranche is not stated, and that interim cash interest and tax are not supplied.
### Key findings

The refinancing in March 2026 changed the shape of the debt. The company issued USD 700 million of 7.875% senior notes due 2034 and used the proceeds with cash to retire the notes due 2027 and part of the notes due 2028, so the next material maturities are the 2028 euro term loan and notes and the 2029 notes, together about USD 1,368 million, or about 35% of USD 3,872 million of debt principal [CP-1 debt table; Calculations]. This removes a near-term wall that the 10-K had flagged as unfunded absent refinancing, at the price of a higher stated coupon on the replacement paper than on the notes retired.

Leverage fell during 2026 but remains high, and management's own targets slipped. Management net leverage was about 4.9x at March 31, about 4.4x at June 30 and about 4.3x at September 30, 2026, driven by debt repaid from Kuan Yin land-sale proceeds rather than by earnings growth [CP-1 quarterly trajectory]. Over the same releases the full-year Adjusted EBITDA range was cut from USD 800 to 900 million to USD 775 to 800 million and the year-end leverage target moved from below 3.8x to below 4.2x. A creditor should treat the improvement as asset-sale deleveraging, which cannot repeat once the land is sold.

Earnings quality is weaker than the headline. Third-quarter 2026 net income of USD 196 million includes a USD 150 million insurance-related receipt booked against SG&A and a USD 50 million land gain, and full-year GAAP results include a USD 307 million nine-month tax provision after a full valuation allowance [CP-1 financials table]. Adjusted EBITDA of USD 200 million excludes these items, but it also excludes litigation and environmental charges that consume cash over 15 to 25 years. Segment mix has shifted: Titanium Technologies Adjusted EBITDA rose to USD 85 million from USD 25 million on price, while Thermal and Specialized Solutions fell to USD 136 million from USD 194 million as the stationary aftermarket normalised after prior-year channel fill [CP-1 segment table].

Legacy obligations sit outside the leverage ratio and compete with debt service. Accrued litigation of USD 553 million and environmental remediation of USD 805 million at September 30, 2026 are not debt, yet the New Jersey order (USD 875 million over 25 years) and the North Carolina settlement (USD 455 million over 15 years, first payment of USD 51 million in October 2026) require annual cash [CP-1A transaction summary]. Part is funded by a USD 150 million insurance escrow and shared with DuPont and Corteva under the 2021 MOU, up to a cap. Including the reserves in debt on an illustrative basis raises leverage to about 6.1x (Calculations); that is a sensitivity, not a measure management or any covenant uses.

Liquidity is adequate on the balance-sheet date but its second leg is uncertain. Unrestricted cash of USD 698 million plus revolver availability of USD 953 million gave USD 1,651 million at September 30, 2026. A USD 220 million revolving tranche matured on October 7, 2026, and the filings do not say whether it was extended. If it was not, arithmetic availability would be USD 733 million. The revolver also carries a springing maturity linked to the 2028 and 2029 debt, so access to the revolver depends on that refinancing being completed in advance.

Cash generation covers interest but not by a wide margin. LTM free cash flow is about USD 211 million (Calculations) against USD 274 million of LTM net interest expense, with FCF flattered by the net USD 50 million of insurance escrow receipt over related settlement payments inside operating cash flow. Management's own full-year free cash flow guide is USD 120 to 160 million, and after dividends of roughly USD 50 million per year the margin for settlement payments and voluntary debt reduction is narrow.

Ratings and market signals confirm the pressure. Moody's downgraded to B1 from Ba3 on July 17, 2026 with a stable outlook; the only S&P statement in the sources is a stale April 16, 2025 affirmation of BB- with negative outlook. The sources contain no market quotes or spreads, so no market-implied view is offered.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. Liquidity is solid at the reporting date: USD 698 million of unrestricted cash, no revolver borrowings and USD 953 million of availability, with management stating that sources are sufficient through at least the end of November 2027 [Management Language, CP-1 liquidity bridge]. The maturity profile has been extended: the senior secured term loan in dollars is due in October 2032 and no bond matures before November 2028 [Documentary Fact]. Customer concentration is low, with no customer above 10% of net sales and about 2,400 customers across about 110 countries [Documentary Fact, CP-1A]. Demand drivers are partly regulatory (AIM Act and F-Gas transitions to Opteon) and partly price-led recovery in TiO2, with growth in Performance Solutions serving data center and semiconductor markets [Documentary Fact for the regulation, Management Language for growth claims]. The company has acted creditor-supportively on capital allocation, cutting the dividend and repaying debt from asset sales [Documentary Fact, CP-1A].

Weaknesses. Leverage is high on any basis shown and the improvement came from asset-sale proceeds [Analyst Interpretation, CP-1 bridges]. Legacy PFAS and environmental liabilities are large, multi-decade and uncertain in scale, and only part is cost-shared [Documentary Fact]. Earnings are concentrated in a cyclical product (TiO2) and a regulation-timed product (Opteon aftermarket) whose year-over-year trend turned negative in the third quarter [Documentary Fact, Analyst Interpretation]. Reported GAAP results are volatile because of litigation, valuation allowance and gain items, which complicates covenant and add-back reading [Documentary Fact]. The financing documents are not in the pack, so guarantor coverage, restricted-payment capacity and covenant headroom cannot be verified [Insufficient Information]. A history of restated prior periods and a past Audit Committee review raise the weight a creditor should place on reconciling adjusted measures to filings [Documentary Fact, Analyst Interpretation].
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity |

| Legacy settlement cash outflows | Annual New Jersey and North Carolina payments and EPA-related spending are fixed in time and sit outside management net debt, so they reduce cash available for debt reduction without changing the reported ratio | Slower deleveraging and a larger refinancing need in 2028 and 2029 if earnings weaken | Critical |

| Refinancing of 2028 and 2029 debt | The euro term loan and 2028 notes, and the 2029 notes, are due within about 25 months of the September 30, 2026 balance sheet; the revolver has a springing maturity tied to them | Market access at a B1 rating decides revolver availability and cost of debt | Material |

| TiO2 price durability | Titanium Technologies earnings improved on price actions; a reversal would remove the main driver of year-over-year Adjusted EBITDA growth | Leverage would rise; interest cover is already thin | Material |

| TSS aftermarket normalisation and seasonality | After prior-year channel fill, Opteon volume is lower; fourth-quarter guidance points to a seasonal decline | Lower segment margin and volatility in cash flow | Material |

| Revolver capacity after October 7, 2026 | One-fifth of commitments matured; post-maturity availability is not stated | Liquidity headroom could be about USD 220 million lower than reported | Material |

| Covenant and legal capacity opacity | The revolver-only secured net leverage test and baskets are described only in summaries; the test level after the quarter ended September 30, 2026 is not stated | Headroom cannot be measured | Material |
| Reporting reliability of adjusted measures | Large exclusions, prior-period revisions and a past internal review | Add-backs may not map to Credit Agreement definitions | Minor |
| Interest rate and euro exposure | The dollar term loan is floating at an effective 7.4%; euro-denominated debt remains | Higher rates or currency moves raise interest burden | Minor |
## Calculations
All figures are USD millions unless stated. CP-1 supplied the inputs; the results below are new to CP-2 and are my calculations.
| Calculation | Inputs | Result |
| Maturity concentration, 2028 | Euro term loan 153 plus 2028 notes 595, over total debt principal 3,872 | 748, or 19.3% |
| Maturity concentration, 2029 | 2029 notes 620 over 3,872 | 16.0% |
| 2028 plus 2029 combined | 748 plus 620 | 1,368, or 35.3% of principal |
| Other instruments (finance leases, financing obligation, supplier financing, other) | 43 plus 91 plus 12 plus 17 = 163 over 3,872 | 4.2% |
| Secured term loans gross, over LTM Adjusted EBITDA (proxy, not a covenant test) | (1,041 plus 153) = 1,194 over 744 | 1.60x |

| Secured term loans net of unrestricted cash (proxy, not a covenant test) | (1,194 less 698) = 496 over 744 | 0.67x. The revolver test uses Credit Agreement definitions that are not supplied, so covenant headroom is Not calculable |
| LTM cash from operations | FY2025 264 plus nine months 2026 263 less nine months 2025 127 | 400 |
| LTM capital expenditure | FY2025 213 plus nine months 2026 144 less nine months 2025 168 | 189 |
| LTM free cash flow | 400 less 189 | 211, or 5.4% of debt principal (211 over 3,872) |
| LTM EBITDA less capex over LTM net interest | (744 less 189) = 555 over 274 | 2.03x |

| Illustrative leverage including reserves | Net debt 3,174 plus accrued litigation 553 plus environmental remediation 805 = 4,532 over 744 | 6.09x. Sensitivity only: reserves are partly discounted, partly cost-shared and not debt; not a management or covenant measure |
| Guidance-implied EBITDA less capex less net interest, 2026 | Low: 775 less 230 less 280; high: 800 less 220 less 275 | 265 to 305, before cash taxes, settlement payments and dividends |
| Dividend burden | Quarterly 0.0875 per share on about 150.5 million shares, four quarters | about 53 per year; the 10-K cites about 50 per year |
## Gaps
| Gap | Why it matters | Affects | Severity | Action |

| Revolver capacity after the October 7, 2026 maturity of the 220 tranche is not stated | Liquidity could be lower than reported | Liquidity, covenant capacity | High | Obtain a later filing or issuer statement |

| Credit Agreement, indentures and guarantor schedules not supplied; covenant definitions, levels after September 30, 2026 and headroom are unknown | Distribution capacity, collateral and structural subordination cannot be verified | Financial risk, creditor control | High | Obtain executed documents |
| Cash paid for interest and taxes in 2026 interim periods not supplied | Cash-basis coverage cannot be measured | Cash flow quality | Medium | Mark as not supplied; use FY2025 only |

| Total FY2025 Adjusted EBITDA is not printed in the sources; segment build differs from the LTM-implied figure | Leverage history cannot be rebuilt precisely | Leverage trend | Medium | Use LTM as attributed |

| Debt-like items outside management net debt (litigation, environmental, sold receivables, supplier finance) are not netted; securitization and factoring balances not quantified | Adjusted leverage is understated by management measure | Leverage | Medium | CP-3 and later modules should show both bases |
| No market data, quotes or spreads; S&P action stale | Market-implied view cannot be formed | Not applicable to this fundamental view | Low | Not required for CP-2 |
| Ownership and holder detail not disclosed | Support behaviour cannot be assessed beyond documented actions | Governance | Low | State as not disclosed |
| Fixed versus variable cost structure and contract share of revenue not disclosed | Margin resilience to a volume decline is not quantifiable | Business risk | Medium | State as not disclosed |
| Illustrative leverage including reserves mixes discounted and undiscounted items | The 6.09x sensitivity is indicative only | Financial risk | Low | Use as a sensitivity, not a metric |
## Next module

CP-5 composes the report from the CP-1, CP-1A and CP-2 handoffs. It should carry the Medium confidence, the revolver and covenant opacity, and the legacy settlement obligations that sit outside management net debt.
